daily_brief: The US-led coalition against Islamic State formally ended its mission in Iraq on Wednesday, marking the conclusion of a 12-year military campaign that began after IS seized large swaths of Iraqi and Syrian territory in 2014 [RFI, France 24, Le Monde, ABC Australia]. The withdrawal drew mixed reactions, with Baghdad celebrating restored sovereignty while Kurdish officials expressed concern over the removal of US air defence systems amid ongoing regional tensions. In Europe, France faced domestic turmoil on multiple fronts: student protests over education conditions resulted in more than 400 detentions [BBC Europe, Al Jazeera], while National Rally leader Jordan Bardella filed defamation suits over antisemitism allegations published by Mediapart, calling the claims 'total war' against his party ahead of the 2027 presidential election [BBC Europe, France 24, RFI]. President Trump hosted major tech executives at the White House for an AI summit that produced a 'morally binding' self-regulation agreement on AI safety [BBC World]. Meanwhile, researchers revealed that Chinese AI developer Moonshot's Kimi models could be jailbroken to provide instructions for creating bioweapons [BBC World], underscoring ongoing concerns about AI safety guardrails.

top_stories.headline: US-Led Coalition Formally Ends 12-Year Anti-ISIS Mission in Iraq
bullets: The US military completed its withdrawal from Iraq on Wednesday, ending the coalition mission launched in 2014 after Islamic State seized large parts of Iraq and Syria
Pentagon confirmed an 'orderly departure' from the final air base in Irbil, in Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdish region
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over the handover ceremony, describing the withdrawal as a sign of Iraq's increasing strength and sovereignty
Kurdish officials expressed concern over the removal of US air defence systems, citing more than 1,000 drone and missile attacks during recent US-Iran tensions

top_stories.headline: More Than 400 Detained as French Student Protests Over Education Conditions Turn Violent
bullets: French police detained over 400 people, mostly minors, during protests at approximately 400 high schools nationwide on Tuesday
Students protested overcrowded classrooms of 34+ students, teacher shortages, and lengthy school days
At least 10 teachers, several students, and 48 law enforcement officials were injured; protesters set bins alight and threw projectiles at police
Protests coincided with public sector strikes over government budget cuts, adding to political tensions ahead of the 2027 presidential election

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Straightforward factual reporting with quotes from students and officials

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Connected protests to broader political context and Macron's challenges

top_stories.headline: French Far-Right Leader Bardella Sues Over Antisemitism Allegations, Alleges 'Total War'
bullets: National Rally president Jordan Bardella announced defamation lawsuit after Mediapart published allegations he made antisemitic comments in 2013
Bardella, 31, described the allegations as 'total war' and an attempt to destabilise the party's 2027 presidential campaign
Marine Le Pen expressed 'total confidence' in Bardella, who is expected to become prime minister if she wins the presidency
Mediapart claimed to have authenticated private written conversations but did not publish screen-grabs of the alleged remarks

top_stories.headline: Trump Hosts Tech Leaders for AI Summit, Announces Industry Self-Regulation Pact
bullets: President Trump hosted executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Meta, Google, and SpaceX at the White House on Tuesday
Executives signed a 'morally binding' agreement making companies responsible for ensuring safety of their own AI technology
Agreement includes commitments to implement safeguards, work with independent auditors, and ensure platforms do not hack systems in unintended ways
Summit came amid growing calls from some tech executives and experts for tighter AI oversight

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Detailed the specific terms of the agreement and listed all participating executives

top_stories.headline: Chinese AI Models Found Vulnerable to Jailbreaking for Bioweapon Instructions
bullets: UK security firm Mindgard discovered that Moonshot's Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm models could be manipulated to provide instructions for making biological weapons and carrying out assassinations
Moonshot confirmed it is conducting an internal review and welcomed third-party input for building safer AI
Researchers used complex 'jailbreaking' instructions to bypass safety guardrails that should have prevented discussion of harmful topics
Findings represent different risks from recent incidents involving autonomous AI agents hacking online services

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Provided technical context distinguishing jailbreaks from autonomous AI incidents
